title: How polychromy research approaches original appearance
description: This photograph shows a modern experimental reconstruction of Phrasikleia, a different Greek sculpture. It is not a result produced by Color Study. The Met’s Chroma exhibition explains reconstructions informed by analytical techniques and historical research, including work on its sphinx.
author: Aquaplaning
modifications: Resized photographic preview; unmodified source JPEG retained.

title: Amenemhat’s painted tomb
description: Egypt’s Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities describes the tomb’s wall scenes and decorated ceiling. These photographs show their surviving condition under artificial lighting.

title: The NASA Spinoff story
description: The article describes decorrelation stretch applied at Angkor Wat and Beni Hassan. Color Study independently implements RGB covariance analysis; it does not reproduce all DStretch color spaces.

title: One restored painting, several photographs
description: The Louvre identifies the painting as restored and records its findspot in court 106 of the palace at Mari. Compare the three views while keeping reflections and restored areas in mind.

title: Paintings moved from a cathedral
description: The National Museum in Warsaw explains the Nubian rescue campaign and presents the paintings in relation to their former architectural setting. A detached fragment’s current display is part of its history.

title: The decorated rooms of Villa A
description: The archaeological park describes Villa A at Oplontis, its phases and surviving decoration. The site’s name and association with Poppaea are not an identification of a painter.

title: From villa walls to museum panels
description: The archaeological park documents excavation and the removal of frescoes for preservation. The present photograph records a panel after that history, including surviving losses.

title: Cacaxtla’s painted political world
description: INAH describes the Epiclassic mural program and its combinations of central Mexican and Maya imagery. Multiple views here belong to one site.

title: A surviving Maya mural program
description: INAH places these paintings in the building commissioned by Chan Muwan II in the late eighth century. The source discusses scenes and their architectural setting.

title: The doors and their collecting history
description: The British Museum records the commission for the Ogoga of Ikere, Olowe of Ise’s authorship and the doors’ transfer after the 1924 British Empire Exhibition.
